description.value: The study examined brain activation, heart rate variability, and their temporal and predictive relationships during paced breathing and psychosocial stress.

spans.text: During MRI-scanning, participants performed a paced-breathing and stress induction task.

design.value: Each participant underwent a single MRI-scanning session involving unpaced breathing, normal-paced breathing, deep-paced breathing, the Montreal Imaging Stress Task, and recovery deep-paced breathing, with fMRI, photoplethysmography, and respiration recorded.

task_description.value: The task consisted of unpaced breathing, normal-paced breathing, deep-paced breathing, the Montreal Imaging Stress Task, and recovery deep-paced breathing.

spans.text: The task begins with 4 min of normal breathing, where participants are free to breathe at their own pace (“unpaced breathing”). Following this, participants are instructed via a visual cue to breathe at a normal rate of 10 breaths/min for 4 min (“normal paced breathing”). This block serves as the control condition for the following block of deep-paced breathing (4 min with a breathing frequency of 5.5 breaths/min).

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to follow a paced breathing exercise and solve arithmetic tasks, submitting responses via a response button box.

spans.text: Participants must solve simple arithmetic tasks (f.ex.: 145–17 + 3) and submit their response via a response button box.

stimuli.value: Simple arithmetic problems and visual feedback regarding correctness and relative performance.

spans.text: Following each trial, participants receive feedback on the submitted response (“correct,” “incorrect” or “too slow”) as well as regarding their own average performance relative to the average performance of all other participants

description.value: 40 oblique interleaved slices were acquired parallel to the AC-PC axis using a T2*-sensitive single-shot EPI sequence; 500 images were collected during one single run. High-resolution T1 MPRAGE images were also acquired.

spans.text: 40 oblique interleaved slices were acquired parallel to the AC-PC axis using a T2*-sensitive single-shot EPI sequence with following parameters: TR = 2500 ms, TE = 26 ms, flip angle = 80°, field of view = 154 × 154 mm with a matrix size of 96 × 96, in-plane resolution of 2.3 × 2.3 × 3.4mm 3 . A total of 500 images were collected during one single run.

description.value: fMRI preprocessing included exclusion of the first four volumes, slice time correction, realignment and unwarping, coregistration, normalization to MNI space, and smoothing.

spans.text: The following pre-processing steps were used: Exclusion of first four volumes to account for magnetic field for equilibration, slice time correction, realignment and unwarping to correct for artifacts due to susceptibility-by-movement interactions, coregistration of T1 images with the mean T2* images, normalization to MNI space (functional: 3mm3, anatomical: 1mm3), smoothing of functional images (8 mm Gaussian kernel).
Pre-processing and statistical analyses of fMRI data were conducted using SPM12 (Wellcome Trust, London, UK).

interpretations.value: The contrast specifically reflects differences between stress and the relaxation response induced by deep-paced breathing.

spans.text: we aimed to isolate stress-related brain activity and eliminate non-specific effects related to visual stimulation or guided breathing.

record.analyses_note: Additional reported analyses include Stress Recovery Specific Relaxation, Post Stress Relaxation, IBI and RMSSD GLM effects, stress/anxiety regressions, GAM analyses for each ROI and HRV measure, hemispheric insula GAM analyses, and bidirectional Granger-causality analyses; these are not separately enumerated here due to output-size constraints.
